text: 'Ralph believes the tallest spy is dangerous,' read de dicto, means:
choices: Ralph believes, of whoever uniquely satisfies the description 'the tallest spy,' that they are dangerous — without necessarily knowing who that is
There is a specific person, the tallest spy, of whom Ralph believes that he is dangerous
Ralph is representing himself in a first-personal (de se) way
'Tallest spy' can be freely replaced by any co-referring term without changing the truth value
explanation: On the de dicto reading the description falls within the scope of 'believes': Ralph believes that whoever is the tallest spy is dangerous, even if he cannot identify the person. Option 1 is the de re reading (a specific individual); option 2 is the de se (first-person); option 3 describes the substitutivity that holds in transparent de re contexts, not in opaque de dicto ones.
